summary: Cloud Build repositories (2nd generation) added support for creating manual triggers, webhook triggers, and Pub/Sub triggers.
extended_definition: Cloud Build repositories (2nd generation) added support for creating manual triggers, webhook triggers, and Pub/Sub triggers.

supporting_pages.title: Create and manage build triggers \_|\_ Cloud Build \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: You can directly create triggers for your repositories in Cloud Source Repositories without manually connecting to them.

Click Create to save your build trigger. gcloud To create a trigger if your source code is in Cloud Source Repositories : gcloud builds triggers create cloud-source-repositories \ --repo= REPO NAME \ --branch-pattern= BRANCH PATTERN \ # or --tag-pattern= TAG PATTERN --build-config= BUILD CONFIG FILE \ --service-account= SERVICE ACCOUNT \ --require-approval Where: REPO NAME is the name of your repository.
This page explains how to connect to source repositories such as GitHub and Bitbucket, and create build triggers to build the code in the repositories.

supporting_pages.title: "Automate builds in response to Pub/Sub events \_|\_ Cloud Build \_|\_ Google\
evidence_snippets: To clone and build repositories through your external source code management system, see Creating and managing build triggers to learn how to specify a build configuration inline.
Note: Pub/Sub triggers cannot build GitHub Enterprise, Bitbucket Data Center, and Bitbucket Server repositories through Cloud Build's native integration.
To disable this behavior, we recommend using manual approvals to gate builds when making pull requests on public repositories.

supporting_pages.title: "Automate builds in response to webhook events \_|\_ Cloud Build \_|\_ Google\
evidence_snippets: Repository triggers that use Cloud Build repositories (2nd gen) can be configured programmatically and are natively integrated with source providers, including support for GitHub and GitLab.
Note: If you're creating a trigger that automates builds on repository events, we recommend using Cloud Build repository triggers.
With webhook triggers, you can define an inline build configuration file rather than specify a source when creating your trigger.
